div.div: The final stop before the packet leaves the network card. This is where SNAT/Masquerade happens (changing the Pod's IP to the Node's IP).

path.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: In Kubernetes, PREROUTING is the most important chain. Why? Because it handles the Service IP translation.

path.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Once the destination is set to a Pod IP, the packet enters the FORWARD chain.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(#ffffff, var(--ge-dark-color, #121212)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 178px; height: 1px; padding-top: 305px; margin-left: 1731px;

div.div: This is where Network Policies usually live.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(#ffffff, var(--ge-dark-color, #121212)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 418px; height: 1px; padding-top: 370px; margin-left: 1491px;

div.div: A Pod has a private IP (e.g., 192.168.1.5); the Internet can't reply to it. The Solution: POSTROUTING performs Masquerading (SNAT), stamping the node's primary private IP over the Pod's IP; a NAT gateway or public IP handles the Internet hop.

div.div: At the Entry (PREROUTING)

div.div: As the packet hits the gate, the "Switchboard" (DNAT) asks Conntrack: "Have I seen this conversation before?"

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(240, 163, 10), rgb(154, 88, 0)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(189, 112, 0), rgb(193, 127, 31));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 303px; height: 1px; padding-top: 460px; margin-left: 1101px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ededed); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: If No (New Packet): Conntrack creates a new entry in its ledger

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(240, 163, 10), rgb(154, 88, 0)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(189, 112, 0), rgb(193, 127, 31));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 438px; height: 1px; padding-top: 560px; margin-left: 1111px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ededed); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: If Yes (Reply Packet): Conntrack says, "I remember this! This is the reply for Pod A," and it automatically rewrites the IP addresses without having to look through the complex rules again.

path.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#ffffff, #121212); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: At the Exit (POSTROUTING)

rect.style: fill: light-dark(#ffffff, var(--ge-dark-color, #121212)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 393px; height: 1px; padding-top: 610px; margin-left: 646px;

div.div: As the packet leaves, Conntrack notes the "return address" (the Node's IP) so it knows exactly which Pod to give the answer to when it eventually comes back.

path.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

rect.style: fill: light-dark(#ffffff, var(--ge-dark-color, #121212)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Linux Kernel has 3 gates to contro the flow of packets.
They exist even without Kubernetes

path.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

rect.style: fill: light-dark(#ffffff, var(--ge-dark-color, #121212)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 636px; height: 1px; padding-top: 150px; margin-left: 733px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
The Linux Kernel has a subsystem called Netfilter. This subsystem is built directly into the operating system.
Netfilter Hooks: These are the "gates" we discuss below. They are hard-coded locations in the Linux networking stack where the kernel pauses for a microsecond to ask, "Does anyone have a rule for this packet?

path.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

rect.style: fill: light-dark(#ffffff, var(--ge-dark-color, #121212)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 478px; height: 1px; padding-top: 150px; margin-left: 1461px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Conntrack: This is a kernel module (nf_conntrack) that provides the "ledger" or state table. It tracks every connection passing through the machine, regardless of whether that machine is a laptop, a web server, or a K8s node.

path.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

rect.style: fill: light-dark(#ffffff, var(--ge-dark-color, #121212)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 308px; height: 1px; padding-top: 130px; margin-left: 2021px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: If you have a fresh Linux server with no apps, those gates are "empty." They exist, but they don't have any specific instructions.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(#ffffff, var(--ge-dark-color, #121212)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 552px; height: 1px; padding-top: 130px; margin-left: 2417px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
When you install Kubernetes, the kube-proxy component starts writing the instructions:
Kube-proxy uses tools like iptables or nftables to tell the Kernel: "When a packet hits the PREROUTING gate and its destination is this Service VIP, use Conntrack to pick a Pod and rewrite the address (DNAT)."
